description.summary: A mythical bird that lays perfectly square or cubic eggs, nesting exclusively on steep hillsides where the geometric eggs won't roll away.
description.full: The Gillygaloo is a fearsome critter from American lumberjack folklore of the northern forests. This peculiar bird has evolved to lay square or cubic eggs rather than round ones, solving the problem of eggs rolling away from nests on steep mountain slopes. According to the tall tales, the Gillygaloo nests only on the steepest hillsides, where round eggs would be impossible to keep in place. The square eggs can be hard-boiled and used as dice, or so the lumberjacks claimed. This absurd adaptation represents classic occupational humor designed to test the credulity of greenhorn workers.
